'''Clausen''' is a [[Danish language|Danish]] [[patronymic]] surname, literally meaning ''child of Claus'', Claus being a [[German language|German]] form of the [[Greek language|Greek]] Νικόλαος, Nikolaos, (cf. [[Nicholas]]), used in Denmark at least since the 16th century.<ref>Søndergaard, Georg (2000) Danske For- og Efternavne. Askholms Forlag. {{ISBN|87-90721-17-9}}</ref> The spelling variant '''Klausen''' has identical pronunciation (as does the often interchangeable '''Claussen''').
The two variants are number 34 and 85 on the top 100 of surnames in Denmark.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.danskernesnavne.navneforskning.ku.dk/Topnavne/Topnavn_reg10_s2_l.asp |title=University of Copenhagen – Name Research Section |access-date=2007-11-10 |archive-date=2009-07-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703191033/http://www.danskernesnavne.navneforskning.ku.dk/topnavne/topnavn_reg10_s2_l.asp |url-status=dead}}</ref> Occurrences of Clausen/Klausen as a surname outside Denmark and [[Schleswig-Holstein]] are due to [[immigration]]. Immigrants to English-speaking countries sometimes changed the spelling to [[Clauson]].
